page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.8xlarge is a storage-oriented general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 1919 GB of local SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets, which assist with vector calculations and neural network instructions.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.i3g.8xlarge demonstrates moderate multi-core capabilities but exhibits lower single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression benchmarks place the instance in the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded operations, such as the stress-ng multi-core test and bzip3 decompression, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes, consistently align with middle-tier performance. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also register average throughput, reflecting a stable profile for transactional workloads.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high local storage density relative to its compute resources. While single-threaded performance is a notable tradeoff, the dedicated CPU allocation and bundled 1919 GB SSD make it a viable option for workloads requiring local data persistence without the overhead of external block storage. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, NoSQL databases, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose applications that benefit from localized storage and moderate multi-threaded processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.8xlarge is a storage-focused general-purpose server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 1919 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on a KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance delivers a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff: single-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%, while multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently achieve average tier results. This hardware profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for storage-heavy workloads that do not require high single-threaded speed. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose applications requiring substantial local storage.
